transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-24
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Nadia Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Das (Redwood CSM), Maria Ortega (NovaCare Platform Lead), Ben Chu (NovaCare SRE), Alan Price (Dir Product), Samira Khan (Security)

Summary (auto): Weekly pilot sync — focus on surge behavior, cutover governance, fallback policies, and telemetry.

[00:00] Jordan: okay, everyone, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep to 45 minutes but there's a few bits, um, updates. quick roll call?
[00:10] Maria: Maria here.
[00:12] Ben: Ben.
[00:13] Alan: Alan, hi.
[00:15] Samira: Samira here.
[00:18] Jordan: great. Nadia and I will run through the canary gating proposal, then go through fallback flows and telemetry thresholds. Nadia, you want to start?
[00:28] Nadia: yeah sure. so quick recap — the pilot is currently hitting about 120 rps sustained in the lab and we've seen 50ms median token latency on the long prompts, uh, with KV cache warm. when we spike to 400 rps we see tails go up to 700-900ms and that starts to violate the product SLOs.
[00:45] Ben: yeah in prod our user distribution is spikier because of batch upload jobs so the 400 number is realistic. question — are you folks recommending a hard traffic gate at X p95 or a gradual throttle?
[01:02] Nadia: good question. the recommendation in the draft is a two-tier gate:
 - canary gate 1 at 95th token-latency 200ms for 5m window, failover to canary variant if breached
 - canary gate 2 is a throughput gate: sustained queue length or request latency store; if breached for 2m, shift 20% traffic to a smaller model variant (quantized) and 10% to a cached-response mode.
this gives us a controlled degradation. note: smaller model is just emb-optimized variant with lower context and cheaper tokens.
[01:40] Maria: and when you say "cached-response mode" that's our prefix cache correct, is that safe for PHI? Samira, question for security — is prefix caching allowed if we mask user identifiers?
[01:53] Samira: we can allow prefix caching for non-PHI cohorts; for PHI we need KMS attestations and audit logging. also we need an answer on retention: NovaCare policy is 30 days ephemeral. Jordan, do you have the KMS integration doc link?
[02:06] Jordan: yes, I will share our KMS + HSM integration doc after the call — short link: https://redwood.app/security/kms-integration (note: that's internal link for the demo). I'll also attach SOC2 artifact list.
[02:18] Alan: back on the gating — if we shift 20% to smaller model, is there an automated rollback if errors or hallucinations spike?
[02:27] Nadia: yes, we wire the canary to three signals: error rate, hallucination detector eval (we run a quick topical classifier), and latency. each signal has a threshold; if any of the primary safety signals exceed the threshold for two consecutive windows we auto-rollback traffic to the previous stable model and trigger an incident page.
[02:43] Ben: what's the page routing? we want pages to our SRE not Redwood on-call for first triage.
[02:50] Priya: we recommend initial paging to NovaCare SRE with Redwood in cc; for the pilot phase Redwood will join the war-room. we'll update runbook with escalation flow.
[02:59] Maria: ok good. can you walk through an example ramp? like from 50 rps to burst 600 rps in 10 minutes?
[03:07] Nadia: sure — plan is to do synthetic ramp tests: 10% increments every 60s to target RPS while keeping canary checks. at each increment we check p95 latency and error_rate; if p95 exceeds 300ms at any step we pause and hold at last good step and then run cache warmup. if that doesn't recover within 2 minutes we kick the fallback policy.
[03:28] Jordan: to be explicit about fallback ordering: 1) client-side token bucket throttle (recommended SDK snippet will reject/queue), 2) server-side route to smaller model variant, 3) server-side serve from prefix cache / best-effort canned answers, 4) degrade to synchronous short-context variant.
[03:44] Ben: client-side throttling — can we get that implemented quick? we control the client.
[03:48] Jordan: yep, we'll send an SDK patch with example token-bucket settings and sample code. we'll also include a feature flag for immediate toggling.
[03:55] Maria: telemetry — what dashboards and alerts should we add? we already have Datadog and a prometheus collector in front of the ingress.
[04:03] Nadia: we recommend three alert groups: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate (5xx/overflow errors), and behavior/regression (score from hallucination classifier). alerts should have two severities: warning (auto-scale + notify SRE) and critical (pause canary + page). For dashboards we'll share a Kibana/Datadog panel JSON.
[04:22] Samira: important: we need audit events for any fallback decision (who toggled, trigger metric values). is that captured?
[04:29] Jordan: yes — all fallback decisions are logged to the audit stream with trace ids; we can forward those to your SIEM (Splunk) via secure forwarder.
[04:36] Alan: quick question on model variants — are the smaller variants the same weights but quantized or a different architecture?
[04:42] Nadia: mostly quantized variants and shorter-context checkpoints; we might also have an optimized decoder-only variant for fast short answers. we tabled the exact mapping in the runbook doc.
[04:51] Ben: ok, about the runbook — is there a preflight checklist we can run before the cutover?
[04:55] Priya: yes, preflight will include: verify KV cache warm, run synthetic ramp to 120% expected peak, validate alert hooks, confirm KMS test key rotation, and confirm rollback toggle works. we'll push a checklist to the runbook page.
[05:10] Maria: when do we do the first full surge test with our real data set?
[05:12] Jordan: we propose next Tuesday 2025-07-29 at 02:00 PT — this will be a 2-hour window with NovaCare SRE, Redwood SE, and CS present.
[05:20] Ben: sounds good. we need the exact traffic shape CSV. Nadia, can you produce that?
[05:25] Nadia: yes I'll generate traffic shapes and a load script — will include cache-warm and cold-run scenarios.
[05:31] Samira: about compliance: we'll need the SOC2 artifact and a short run-through of audit logs retention; I want to see log schema. Jordan?
[05:39] Jordan: I'll include the SOC2 checklist and the log schema (fields, retention) in the follow-up email.
[05:44] Maria: what about cost controls during the surge — we don't want runaway spend if something loops.
[05:49] Nadia: we recommend the budget cap at the routing layer: if cumulative token cost estimate in a 10m window exceeds X, we automatically cap burst and shift to cached variants; Jordan will add sample gating numbers to the pricing doc.
[05:59] Alan: can we have a quick note about observability for model regressions? e.g., a set of seed prompts to validate output quality post-upgrade?
[06:06] Nadia: yes, Redwood Optimize can run a quick eval on a seed set and surface per-model QA diffs. we'll add that to the canary checks: quality delta not exceed 3% on our eval metric.
[06:18] Jordan: okay let's capture immediate action items — Nadia runs 2-hour surge test, Ben provides ingress config, Jordan sends KMS and SOC2 artifacts and pricing for burst, Samira sends compliance Qs to Jordan and Priya. we aim to update runbook with gating thresholds before the surge test.
[06:34] Maria: team, thanks. a couple logistics: please put the runbook link in the calendar invite and we'll confirm attendance for the 7/29 window.
[06:42] Jordan: will do. any other questions?
[06:45] Ben: one more — are the fallback toggles exposed via the console and API?
[06:48] Nadia: yes both. console toggle is for UI operators; API is for infra automation. both create an audit event.
[06:54] Alan: ok great.
[06:56] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with notes and artifacts. meeting end.
